blocks.text: Second Samuel begins the census account by linking David's action with the LORD's anger, while First Chronicles describes the incitement differently, attributing it to an adversary or Satan. Readers have offered harmonizing, developmental, and distinct-source explanations, but no single explanation resolves the difference beyond dispute.

sections.title: A Question Raised by the Opening Verse

blocks.text: Second Samuel traces David's rise and the consolidation of his kingdom, then moves through the ark and dynasty promise, royal abuse, household violence, rebellion, grief, and a four-part closing appendix. This larger shape places the final chapters within a book that holds together both David's kingship and its painful consequences.
